reviews.title: Verses need context

 It has helped me to slow down and see how it’s possible to enjoy the bible in a different way by meditating on verses.  I still have my Bible open when I use the app so that I can see the context of the verses and make notes.  I think that is important. 


I have noticed that sometimes the verses picked to meditate on are completely out of context.  When you read the surrounding verses they are not always appropriate to use in the context intended on the app.  That does spoil it for me.  I think the choice of verses used is important.  More consideration should be given to this.    It’s why I have given it only 3 stars as we have to be carefully about bending the word of God into what we want it to mean.

reviews.title: Can never find topic that is advertised when I click your push notifications
reviews.body:
[Updating a previous very positive review now that my count of devotions heard is up to over 700…(1), I have in 2026 and today still, 4/28/26 been having a  problem a year that an interesting sounding push notification topic  comes up on my iPhone 16e, but when I follow it, it leads to a menu of devotions, and week long study series, —none of which are the subject teased in the notification—Can you have it link directly to the devotion it is advertising? Or at least allow us to search your crammed-full menu? I have a Bible reading plan with my paper Bible I’m lucky to keep up, so I don’t use the “sign up for a week of …” come-ons, really. So my use of the app has fallen significantly though I’m still paying for it, hopefully someone else is gaining satisfaction from the typically well done meditations. Though the breathing and relaxation really doesn’t suit me if I listen in the AM, and I find it all kinda “new age” 

Previous review: Have just lost a paper journal yet again in my house, so the times I’ve “written in my journal” here are also of importance in the wee hours, not bedtime, when I can contemplate & have energy to write at the same time. Have copied some to notes in my iPhone, which I’ve had one of for almost a decade - so maybe more secure than paper? For now anyway. 
(2) Just having listened to the Jenn Stoltzfus / Tyler Bods “I am Loved” devotion, I used it as springboard, with a screenshot of your starry night graphic, on FB; having recalled my Dad using that phrase (1) time to me in my life (we were not a family where “I love you” was said, ever, either: though a good upbringing otherwise.) My suggestion: one problem I have in the Roman’s 8:35-39 journey, which is likely all of our lifetime journals, to see if God ever leaves us, is not the danger / deprivation / illness / storms struggle, nor the power of angels or anything created, except MYSELF. Perhaps it shows narcissism but that scripture leaves put one created thing which I constantly fear WILL show God will or has left me or that I’ve been fooling myself I’m loved: MY OWN FAILURE, amplified by Satan’s semi-true or true accusations… Perhaps a devotion where the pilgrim passes THAT created hurdle would be good. Yeah, I know Paul did address it when he said he was the “chiefest of sinners” but I think we are all, in our failures, and disappointments in ourselves, capable of feeling we are a special case, and even “Chiefer” than Paul… I bet some devotions of this nature will be coming ! You demonstrate God’s power & constancy very well of COURSE. Thanks again

reviews.title: I love this App, BUT...
reviews.body:
I love this app, but I only gave it 3 stars because I think it needs improvements. 

It would be nice to be able to select a playlist of the meditations I like best from ALL of the selections. 

It would be nice to have the option of perpetual play, rather than a maximum of 90 minutes. With the background music/sounds also available for that duration. 

Some of the meditations are louder than others. It would be nice if the volume was equalized. 

For those of us who have subscribed, an offline function would be great. Users could download their playlist within the app, and listen offline. Personally, I listen without ear buds. I have my phone or iPad near my ear so as to not disturb my husband. I don’t like having active wifi that near my head. 

So, I love having Christian meditations and I think this app is the best one out there, but it needs some pretty basic program tweaks to keep me renewing next year. 

I hope to see some developments in the app that are more user friendly.

Despite looking like a great app, I can’t even get past the first page, since when I enter my email and click continue nothing happens. Scrolling through previous reviews (some from over a year ago...) I’ve found the exact same problem has happened to many others. I’m not sure why after countless complaints this malfunction hasn’t been fixed...? I think the app developers just need to be more diligent. It’s ridiculous, and in the end you’re so tired from trying countless times that the app is no longer appealing. N.B. I have also tried to sign in online (using the response of a previous review), only to receive an error message. What a shame.

Often drug addicts don't have money, people on the verge of suicide, aren't going to dig out a credit card and pay for help. I have to wonder if this is a business or a ministry. Perhaps the designers of this app should pray for funding for it or ask for donations from their church, assuming they believe God has called them to do this. I will be removing this from my device and praying for another tool for my friend.

reviews.title: Right out of the gate...
reviews.body:
I’m surprised with the fact that the app description describes an annual fee of $30 which I’m already quite hesitant to pay not because it’s overly expensive, in and of itself, but because there are several Membership situations out there that accumulate to a lot of money per month (e.g. Netflix, Spotify and this app, or that app etc.). Regardless, I thought I’d give it a one year try (as two weeks is simply not a long enough trial period in these modern days of busyness) .  So, when I downloaded the app and got to the page that suggested a membership, the fee was $40 not $30 as advertised. Keep your advertisement current people!
Perhaps, also take a lesson from the TV and music apps. They give access to limited content which allows the new user to choose if they want more but can also enjoy some of the content free from fees. Perhaps you don’t need the business but I think in this way you might also get more subscriptions. Also, TV apps give a longer trial period. I think that this is better for a person trying to make a decision whether or not they’re going to invest in yet another application that requires a subscription. And, for the company’s potential benefit, might also give the person trial’ing enough time to fall in love with it and want to subscribe.
So, my first impressions of the app are disappointing.
